question.problem: Given that ${\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x=A,$ what is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)={x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡(-x) \\  & ={x}^{4}(-\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & =-{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)={x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Finally, using the adjacent intervals rule for integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =0 \\ {\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =0 \\ A+{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =0 \\ {\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-A.\end{aligned}
$$
